## Project rules for coding agents (chipgraph)

These rules come from this repository's chipgraph profile and the organization rules it
extends. Follow them whenever you add or change a file.

### Project and blocks

- Project: `tinysoc`
- Packs: `tinysoc`
- Chip spec: `chip.yml` (format `chip-yaml`)
- Target: asic

Each block is an IP. Its instances are the names the chip's memory map uses for it; a
block with no instances listed matches the instance of the same name.

| Block | Instances |
|---|---|
| `gpio` | - |
| `timer` | - |
| `top` | - |

### Where files go

Create each kind of file only at the path its template gives; do not invent new
directories. In a template, `{block}` is the block name and `{BLOCK}` is the block name in upper case.

| Kind | Path template |
|---|---|
| filelist | `filelists/{block}.f` |
| spec | `doc/specs/TINY_{BLOCK}_MAS.md` |

Per-block overrides:

| Block | Kind | Path template |
|---|---|---|
| `top` | spec | (none) |

### Before you open a PR

Run these from the repository root and fix what they report:

```sh
chipgraph ingest    # build the Design Model; the cross checks read it
chipgraph check     # run every configured check; exits 1 if one fails
chipgraph audit     # every finding, grouped by layer
```

Scope a run with `chipgraph check --block <block>` or `chipgraph check --only <check>`.
`chipgraph ingest --strict` and `chipgraph audit --strict` also exit 1, on an error-level
ingest issue or a blocking finding.

Configured checks (a severity caps what the check reports; a command's `{block}` is the
block name):

| Check | Adapter | Severity | Command |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cdc_struct` | cdc_struct | - | - |
| `connect` | connect | - | - |
| `cross_chip` | cross_chip | - | - |
| `duplicate` | duplicate | - | - |
| `hardcode` | hardcode | - | - |
| `lint` | cmd | - | `make lint BLOCK={block}` |
| `ports_diff` | ports_diff | - | - |
| `spec_schema` | spec_schema | - | - |
| `trace` | trace | - | - |

### Requirement IDs

- A requirement ID in a spec must match `REQ-[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*-\d+`.
- Name the ID in the test that covers it: the `trace` check traces each requirement to a test.
